newsitem.title: UK: Licht cuts 96/97 sugar stocks/demand estimate.
newsitem.headline: Licht cuts 96/97 sugar stocks/demand estimate.

text.p: World sugar stocks should reach 48.44 million tonnes raw value at the end of August 1997, representing 40.21 percent of total demand, German statistician F.O. Licht said in a report on Thursday.

In its third estimate of the 1996/97 world sugar balance, Licht said it had initially expected a rise to 42.27 percent after 39.81 percent last year. In February Licht estimated the stocks/demand ratio at 40.92 percent.
The lower figure reflected the drop in India. Sugar disappearance was forecast at 120.46 million tonnes in 1996/97 after a previous 117.34 million.
Licht said the disappointing trend in consumption had been reversed since 1994/95, with the increase estimated to reach 2.7 per cent in 1996/97.

Factors included the halt in consumption decline in eastern Europe and also in the U.S. substitution process as isoglucose usage there was near saturation point. Consumption growth had also picked up in Brazil after years of stagnation.
